reviews.title: No longer a meditation app
reviews.text:
This app used to be phenomenal for building a real meditation practice back in 2018 or so. Since being bought out by $4B AI health tech company Sword Health, they’ve gutted the core focus on mindfulness and replaced it with a flood of 4-minute snippet personal affirmations.

Years ago, I used Headspace to learn legitimate techniques inspired by traditional buddhist monk training, extending my sits to 30 or 60 minutes with results that changed my life. Now, the app is jam-packed with "mood boosters," white noise, and audio clips for doing jumping jacks. The actual courses on how to meditate have either evaporated or been buried deep under layers of menus.

If you truly want to learn the practice of meditation, look elsewhere. If you want a 3.5-minute mini podcast telling you how to overcome imposter sydrome while the host reminds you to breathe, this app is for you.

[My understanding is this bite-sized content has been designed to pad engagement stats, which fatten Sword Health’s $4B valuation and prep the company for an IPO. as usual $$$ ruins everything]

reviews.title: UX so broken it causes anxiety, zero customer support
reviews.text:
Headspace is going backwards. It causes me a lot of anxiety just trying to get to a session to help with that anxiety — that is a bad irony for an app that’s supposed to help.

Basic user flows are incredibly broken — I can’t imagine that the developers actually use this app daily. There are a number of very basic UI bugs that have persisted for months, and the navigation of content has gotten increasingly confusing.

You can’t investigate a single session without starting it — which adds spam to your session history, recommendations, and Apple Health data even if you pause it after 3 seconds.

Not to mention that the Pause button looks like a Play button, because the UI has been broken for months and the devs refuse to fix it — despite their support team acknowledging that they know about it.

If you find what you’re looking for in the mess (which has no filters or real tools for searching), the sessions can be good, even though the basics of playing a session are surprisingly broken (long loads, reversed UI prompts, a ‘Love’ icon that shows the opposite state, etc.).

Despite the steady stream of bug-fix updates, the basic issues aren’t ever repaired. And reporting bugs has no effect, even when support reps acknowledge that they’re aware of the busted UI.

As a final insult, the app is now spammed with ‘share this with a friend’ prompts. Why would I tell a friend about an app the devs put such little care into actually supporting? It feels like a naked money grab by a team

reviews.title: From lifeline to cluttered redesign
reviews.text:
I used Headspace daily for two years. It was more than an app — it was a structured, thoughtful routine that genuinely helped me through difficult periods.

The previous design was clean and logical. My daily routine appeared top to bottom in a clear sequence: breathing, Wake Up, meditation, afternoon practice, sleep. It felt intentional.

The redesign removed that clarity. The home screen is now cluttered. The daily routine is no longer visually structured, and the layout flows horizontally in a way that makes no intuitive sense. Checkmarks disappeared for completed exercises (recently restored in one section), and streak tracking has become obscure.

Every meditation now defaults to the wrong length. Post-meditation check-ins congratulate me on my “first exercise” after two years of daily use. “Wake Up” content has become repetitive, sometimes repeating the same video on consecutive days. The short reflections at the end of sessions no longer relate to the meditation theme.

Individually these are small issues. Together they signal a loss of curation and coherence.

Support was polite but procedural. I didn’t feel heard, only processed.

Headspace used to be intentional. It now feels product-driven rather than practice-driven.

I’m genuinely disappointed.

reviews.title: Beware the automatic renewal
reviews.text:
This is a decent app, although heavily weighted towards the US market. Recent UI changes have made it less user friendly, unfortunately, and Headspace seem to be slow to respond to the issues raised in multiple reviews (sort by “most recent” to read them). 

If you are uncertain about continuing, I would strongly recommend cancelling long before the automatic subscription comes due. This is possible via the app and you will still receive your full subscription period. 

One reminder email is sent, but it is buried within a heavily increased barrage of emails leading up to renewal. Out of around 50 emails sent across the year, half were sent in the final ten weeks before renewal, including the single reminder notice. 

Caveat emptor.

reviews.text: Headspace works with 3rd party companies to offer long term free trials with what seems to be the hope that you will forget about auto-renewal and get charged for a year subscription. Any other app would handle immediate requests for refunds appropriately, by offering a full refund or at the very least a partial refund. Instead Headspace adamantly denies refunds of any kind even when the request is sent THE SAME DAY of the charges. I signed up for a free 3mo trial, used it for about 3 days maybe, then forgot about it. Today I receive an email notifying me of the renewal charge of $79 and, given my current financial situation, freaked out because I just can’t afford that for an application I never use. Yes I should have cancelled, but life happens and you forget. But let’s not pretend this isn’t a ploy to hopefully collect money from a forgetful customer. It would be one thing if I used the app and even delayed requesting a refund til days or weeks AFTER the charge, with demonstrated usage after renewal… then I’d say yea, no refund should be given at all, because your product was being utilized. But that’s not my case, and $79 in THIS economy is a lot, and it’s absolutely disgusting that a mental health app makes no exceptions for instances like these when most mental health problems people suffer from HAVE EVERYTHING TO DO WITH FINANCIAL STRAIN! Do better, stop the greed, especially while selling us on caring about our mental health.

reviews.title: AI wellness/data collection therapy
reviews.text: Extremely disappointed and concerned that my go-to meditation app recommends talking to and taking suggestions from an AI companion/therapist that acknowledges and agrees with whatever you have to say, basically like an empathetic ChatGPT. Headspace says it's not a substitute for human care, but that's obviously how its going to be used. Headspace also collects data from your conversations to improve the service. My question is: Why is any of this necessary for a wellness app? Knowing the damage social media causes our mental well-being, why is Headspace going ALL IN on the unknown damage effects AI has on our well-being? There are cases where chatbots have encouraged users to take drastic action (do your own research) to their own health risk, never mind the environmental and ethical concerns. I find it insane that Headspace promotes serenity and well-being but then incorporates this technology as soon as it becomes available, with no concern for users. I don't care if they call it "clinical" and "throughouly tested by researchers," it's not healthy.

I have have had similar experiences in the past where companies defaulted to auto-renewal and I asked for it to be reversed and it was never denied. I understand the business wants to grant its revenue, but sneaking a default to auto-renew, despite being common practices, its immoral and just feels like a sneaky dodgy way to take money from us… specially when there is no flexibility to reverse it like in this case.
